title: Put a washed countertop deep fryer back together: pot into the base, control assembly down its two tracks
instruction: Put the deep fryer back together after washing so that it is ready to use.
context: Countertop deep fryers are taken apart and washed after use and put back together before the next. The Presto ProFry manual: "Place removable pot in base. Attach the control assembly to the base by aligning the two guides on the front of the control unit with the two tracks on the back of the base. Slide the control assembly down as far as it goes ... The appliance will only operate when both guides are properly positioned in the tracks." The pot is lifted "grasping two opposite corners". The order is forced: the element hangs 11 cm down inside the pot, so the pot cannot go in after it. The 27 cm pot fits its base with 3 mm to spare, so two hands lower it level; held by one end it tips and falls. The 0.75 kg control assembly must be lifted until its element loop clears the pot's rim, lowered into the pot without knocking it, and its two 5 mm guides slid down two 8 mm tracks to their stops (the interlock).
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, z up from the table. (1) Fryer base, stainless, fixed: outer 20.5 (x) x 30.0 (y), rim 16.0 cm high, walls 1.2 cm, on 1 cm feet; x 30.0 to 50.5, y -15 to 15, back toward the robot, black end handles. On the back wall's outside two tracks at y +-2.5: 8 mm channels between rails (5 mm wide, 6 mm deep) from 6.5 to 15.0 cm high, the top 1 cm flared out 45 deg, red stops at the foot. (2) Pot, enamelled steel, loose, 0.65 kg: 17.5 x 27.0 cm at the top, 16.5 x 26.0 at the bottom, 12.5 cm deep, walls 4 mm, 9 mm flange; starts on the table centred at x 13.5, y 0. Seated it hangs on its flange centred at x 40.25. (3) Control assembly, loose, 0.75 kg: black control unit 5.8 x 7.0 x 11.6 cm under a head 11.2 x 7.0 x 2.9 cm (knob, signal light) reaching 4.6 cm over the rim; two guides (5 mm wide, 5 cm long) on its front; two 9 mm element tubes down to a 12.4 x 10.9 cm loop. It stands on the table, element pointing forward, unit's back at x 20.0, centred y 26.0. Arms at the ready pose, grippers open. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Read every control step from poses, PhysX contact forces and finger points. 0.25: pot seated (flange on the rim within 2 mm in height, within 3 mm across, tilt < 2 deg). 0.5: and both guides' feet inside their track channels. 0.75: and both guides within 2 mm of their stops with the assembly resting on the base with 3 N or more (interlock closed) and the whole element loop inside the pot. 1.0 (success, held 1 s): all that, no finger within 1 cm of pot or assembly, both still (< 1 mm in 1 s). Caps for the rest of the run: the assembly ever pressing on the pot with over 5 N (the element knocking it) caps at 0.75; the assembly dropped (falling faster than 0.7 m/s) or tipped over 45 deg caps at 0.5. Otherwise 0. Real trial: flange flat on the rim (photo), guides down on the stops (photo of the back), loop inside the pot; plug in and turn the thermostat up for a moment: the signal light comes on only with both guides fully down; turn it down and unplug. Knocks, drops and grippers clear judged from the video.
reset_notes: Lift the control assembly straight up out of its tracks and stand it on the table on its element loop, element pointing away from the robot, its back face 20 cm in front of the arm-base line and 26 cm to the left; lift the pot out by two opposite corners and stand it centred 13.5 cm in front of the line. The base stays put. In simulation each trial starts afresh.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 20 Hz control. The base is fixed to the table. The pot's walls are 4 mm (real: about 1 mm steel). Control unit, head and element are one rigid body; the element is drawn as straight 9 mm tubes, its loop a rectangle. The interlock switch is not a part: it is read as both guides standing on their stops with the assembly's weight on the base. No oil, basket, lid or cord. Masses and sizes are estimates for a Presto ProFry-class fryer.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (the right gripper pushed the pot across the table and tipped it; the left gripper hovered near the control assembly; nothing was put into the base); demo: 1.0
